previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for worsening ascites and uncontrolled blood sugars. She underwent a therapeutic and diagnostic paracentesis, removing 0.9 L of fluid without evidence of infection. Her tacrolimus dose was increased to 2.5 mg twice daily to address subtherapeutic levels and prevent rejection, and her insulin regimen was maintained on glargine with a switch to Novolog for sliding scale coverage. Primidone was increased for worsening essential tremor, and megestrol acetate was discontinued due to improved appetite and concerns about fluid retention. Social work coordinated home services and support from her sister. She was discharged home with improved symptoms and follow-up arranged in transplant and neurology clinics.
